To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the education and training of the future workforce in adolescent health is essential to improve adolescent health outcomes.
the education of the future adolescent health workforce should be competency-based, and the competencies should include knowledge, skills, attitudes, and behavior.
competency-based education and assessment tools are the most effective methods to teach and assess adolescent health competencies in preservice and postgraduate training.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a competency-based framework that can be used by health institutions to assess the quality and effectiveness of their teaching and learning in the adolescent health and medicine field.
the development and implementation of a framework to support quality education in adolescent medicine, which will be useful to institutions and individuals teaching adolescent medicine and health.
the following question: What is the best way to teach adolescent health to the future health workforce?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current literature on adolescent health education and training is limited.
the evidence for the quality of education in adolescent health is limited.

adolescent health competencies are not currently well defined and that there is no clear evidence of how to best teach and assess adolescent health competencies in health professions training programs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is an urgent need to educate and train health professionals in adolescent medicine, and that this should be competency-based and delivered by institutions that are adolescent health–focused.
we have identified a number of key competencies that should be included in undergraduate and postgraduate education in adolescent health.
the future of adolescent health education and training is competency based.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need to invest in education in adolescent health, and to develop a conceptual framework to assess and monitor the quality of teaching adolescent health.

adolescent health is a core component of health care and health education and training and that the competencies of the future workforce need to be defined and measured to ensure that they are adequately prepared to care for adolescents.
competency-based education and the development of an adolescent health curriculum are feasible and can be achieved in a variety of settings.
